description: A single .NET global tool that drives C# services on AWS — bootstrap, deploy, and rollback for Lambda, ECS Fargate, static-site, and coupled full-stack targets, all from one committed manifest.
releaseNotes:
- `kanject aws deploy` can put any Lambda entry behind a managed, streaming Function URL and CloudFront, recorded in the ledger (proposal 0048 r3 §9).
  A stage's `http.<entry>` can now be a managed `function-url` with `responseMode: streaming` (Lambda streams past the 6 MB buffered limit), on an entry with the Web Adapter host. The deploy renders `<stack>-http-<entry>`: the Function URL on the entry's `live` alias with both permissions a `NONE` URL needs and, with the optional `cloudFront` block, a distribution in front of it.
  - The distribution uses managed `CachingDisabled` and `AllViewerExceptHostHeader`. It sends an origin-secret header from Secrets Manager, pinned to the version current at each deploy, so rotating is `put-secret-value` and then a deploy. It can carry `GET`/`HEAD`-only methods, a us-east-1 custom domain with Route 53 records, a WAF ACL and response headers added when missing (a Basic `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, which Function URLs rename).
  - The edge is reconciled before promotion when the alias exists, so a failure leaves traffic in place, or after it on a first deploy. It is verified through CloudFront, and the bare URL must refuse a request without the secret at `cloudFront.originCheckPath`, a guarded path that is required and can't be the readiness path the adapter calls without the secret.
  - The ledger records it under `httpEdges`. Rollback audits each edge against a fresh render before moving an alias, and a single-entry weighted rollout canaries through it.
  - Multi-entry services can front any entry. An edge the stage stops declaring is never deleted silently.
  - New codes: `KANCLI572` (certificate or zone) and `KANCLI577` (origin secret); the rest reuse 0048's `KANCLI674–680`.
  - This replaces hand-written edge stacks such as the licence feed's `infra/feed-edge`. Its live proof on AWS is still to come.

- A Lambda entry can declare the Web Adapter host, and kanject wires it (proposal 0048 r3 §9.2).
  `"httpHost": {"kind": "web-adapter"}` on a manifest entry runs ASP.NET Core on Kestrel behind the Lambda Web Adapter, as a Native AOT binary on `provided.al2023`. kanject adds the adapter layer for the stage's region (arm64, pinned at version 30 and checked live before anything builds, `KANCLI579`). It replaces any hand-pinned adapter layer and writes `AWS_LWA_PORT` and `ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS` onto every function it owns. With a managed Function URL (below) it also writes `AWS_LWA_INVOKE_MODE`, the readiness check and the origin secret's id; otherwise the template's own invoke mode stands. The host contract is checked before the build (`KANCLI581`): the entry must be Native AOT, and `Amazon.Lambda.AspNetCoreServer*`, which replaces Kestrel whenever Lambda runs it, must not appear anywhere in its restore closure. That includes packages brought in through a class library; the message gives the `dotnet nuget why` command that finds it. A stage or `entryEnv` that sets one of the adapter's keys is refused (`KANCLI573`), and a stage template kept as written must already carry the adapter (`KANCLI582`).

- The Web Adapter layer is a locked dependency, a hand-written edge can be adopted, and streaming is verified through the edge (proposal 0048 r4 §9.9).
  - Locked adapter. `kanject aws web-adapter upgrade` pins the layer version in `manifest.lock.json`, through `kanject sync` so the lock hash stays consistent. Deploy uses the pinned version and refuses one this CLI hasn't verified (`KANCLI579`). An unpinned or older lock warns `KANCLI578`.
  - Adoption. `kanject aws deploy --adopt-edge <STACK>` moves a hand-written edge's Function URL, permissions and CloudFront distribution into kanject's stack with a validated CloudFormation stack refactor (`KANCLI576`). The distribution keeps its id and domain; Route 53 records stay in the old stack and keep pointing at it. Before anything moves, adoption refuses (naming each setting) if kanject's render of the stage's `http` block would drop an alias, certificate, WAF ACL, response header or origin header, change the allowed methods, or change the URL's mode or auth.
  - Streaming verification. `verification.stream` fetches a large response through CloudFront (bearer or Basic credentials) and checks the time to first byte and the body size. Only a body over 6 MB counts as proof of streaming. `verification.headers` checks headers on the health response. The bare URL must refuse with 401/403; any other failure is recorded unverified.
  - Refused before building. `AWS_LWA_ENABLE_COMPRESSION` with streaming (`KANCLI573`), and a streaming URL on a VPC-attached stage (`KANCLI674`).
  - Warnings. A missing readiness route and Kestrel endpoints set in code or settings (`KANCLI580`), and a `maxResponseBytes` that outlasts the function's timeout (`KANCLI575`).
  - Rollback refuses a target version that doesn't run behind the adapter while an edge serves it (`KANCLI581`).
  - One port. `httpHost.port` renders both Kestrel's and the adapter's port.
  - Dry run and doctor. `--dry-run` prints each streaming edge's limits and cost. `doctor --env` reports each edge's URL invoke mode, auth and alias binding, and the live adapter layer.

- A fresh git worktree builds its cross-repo libraries without fetching them.
  A linked worktree's `.kanject/cache` is gitignored, so it starts empty, and its first build failed `KANBUILD001`. Once a library's `main` had moved, `kanject sync --locked` failed `KANCLI196` too, until someone ran a plain sync or copied `.kanject/` across by hand. `kanject sync` now copies each locked clone that the main checkout's cache already holds, so `kanject sync --offline` in a new worktree needs no network and no library credentials. `KANBUILD001` now names that command, and `KANCLI196` lists each library that moved since the lock was written (`locked a81c0fd, now b04ff21`) and says how to build the committed commits instead.

- `entryEnv` references resolve, and a skipped alias routing says why.
  A stage's per-entry overlay (`entryEnv.<entry>`) now resolves its `secret:` and `param:` values the same way stage `env` does, so a per-entry secret reaches only that entry's function. Through 1.0.79 those values deployed as their literal text, for example `secret:svc/dev/key`. An overlay that reaches the deployer unresolved now stops the deploy (`KANCLI696`) instead of shipping the reference. Separately, when a template sets `Globals.Api` or `Globals.HttpApi`, or declares its own API beside implicit `Api`/`HttpApi` events, `kanject aws deploy` now warns `KANCLI682` and names the cause. kanject leaves that API's events on the function, so rollback and weighted rollouts don't move their traffic. Until now the router skipped them without saying so.

- Under the changelog versioning model, `packages release` honours declared release intents.
  Until now the model ignored `packaging/intent/`. The version rose by `--part`, or by `patch` when nothing was passed, so a declared minor shipped as a patch unless whoever ran the release remembered `--part minor`, and the declaration was left behind. Now:
  - The highest declared part is the default, and `--part` (or the interactive choice, which starts there) can only raise it. A lower `--part` is `KANCLI604`.
  - The release commit deletes the declarations it resolved, and its body records the part and their notes.
  - A version left open by the earlier workflow (an `X.Y.Z - unreleased` heading) releases at its own number, so a run that finds declarations stops with `KANCLI604` instead of dropping them. The release notes still come from the changelog fragments alone.

- Stage files accept an `aws` block.
  It is empty for now and nothing moves into it: it is the place AWS-specific settings land from here on, so that a later schema change can carry the existing top-level AWS fields (`region`, `stack`, `function`, `ecs`, …) under the same key without a migration (proposal 0054). A stage file without the block reads exactly as before.
